newsitem.title: PERU: 300 miners believed trapped by Peruvian earthquake.
newsitem.headline: 300 miners believed trapped by Peruvian earthquake.

text.p: At least 300 miners are believed to be trapped in an underground gold mine after a powerful earthquake shook southern Peru on Tuesday, officials said.

Colonel Lucio Corpuera, a Civil Defense official in Lima, said the miners were trapped inside a mine where 800 people normally work 310 miles (500 km) south of Lima. The quake measuring 7.3 on the Richter scale killed seven people and injured 500 in the region of Nazca.
"We have reports that at the Huanca mine there are some 300 people trapped. It is an informal mine that has apparently suffered landslides," Corpuera told Reuters.
The National Mining Federation in Lima estimated as many as 800 miners were trapped underground by the earthquake that badly damaged the town of Nazca, 290 miles (460 km) south of Lima.
Peru's informal gold miners, who produce 40 percent of the nation's gold, do not belong to registered companies, use little technology and develop their mines in a haphazard way.

"Mostly those working in the mine were small families working separately. Usually they do not know each other, and only see each others' faces when they enter the mine," said Juan Ramirez, the mining federation's general secretary.
